newsitem.title: FRANCE: Press group seeks French help on Lebanese reporter.
newsitem.headline: Press group seeks French help on Lebanese reporter.

text.p: A press freedom watchdog group asked French President Jacques Chirac on Thursday to intercede with Lebanese authorities on behalf of a detained journalist.

"Pierre Atallah is currently being detained because he was pursuing his profession of journalism and because of his opinions," the Paris-based Reporters Without Borders (Reporters sans frontieres - RSF) said in a letter to Chirac.

"RSF is aware of the close ties between France and Lebanon as well as your support for freedom of the press and the friendship uniting you and Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri," the group wrote, urging him to use his influence with the authorities on Atallah's behalf.
The group gave a copy of the letter to Reuters. Chirac's office had no immediate response to the message.

Lebanon's military prosecuter has charged Atallah, a Christian journalist working for Beirut's leading conservative An-Nahar newspaper, with having contacts with Israeli agents and distributing leaflets that incite military disobedience.
He has also been charged with "disturbing Lebanon's relation with a friendly country". If convicted, he would face up to three years in prison.

Atallah was among four dozen individuals detained in the last two weeks after an incident in which a van carrying Syrian workers was machinegunned in a predominantly Christian area of Beirut, killing the driver and injuring some passengers.
Syria has 35,000 troops in Lebanon and is the country's main power broker.
Lebanese officials say that many of those detained have alreay been released.
